how_to_apply: Open the NIT Delhi Project Associate-I Google Form. The notice also prints a QR code that leads to it.

Fill in the application form printed in the notice (Application Form for Project Associate-I in ANRF/ECRG/2025/001559). It asks for personal details, education in reverse chronological order, teaching/industry/research experience, GATE details (year, discipline, score, rank, marks, validity), professional skills, the title of your M.Tech dissertation, up to 250 words on how this position helps your career goal, research publications and two referees.
Sign the form and scan it.
Write your communication address, email address(es) and current contact number(s) correctly.
At the end of the Google Form, upload the signed, scanned application form and the documents listed below as one merged PDF file, with every page self-attested.
Upload your photograph and signature separately as JPEG images.

Incomplete forms, and forms received after the due date and time, will be summarily rejected. The notice also says no delay caused by online processing or poor internet connectivity will be entertained.

content_sections.heading: NIT Delhi Project Associate-I Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Four years B. Tech. Degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering/Computer Science Engineering with first division/class. Preference goes to candidates with experience in: Wireless Communications, Digital Signal Processing MATLAB and Python Machine Learning and Deep Learning Scientific writing and documentation Publications or project experience in communication systems or AI Embedded Systems/SDR/FPGA Check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions for this post.

content_sections.heading: Job Description
content_sections.text: The person selected will: Assist in algorithm development and simulation for wireless communication research. Implement software modules in MATLAB/Python. Support hardware experimentation using SDR/FPGA platforms. Maintain project records, technical documentation and software repositories. Assist in organising workshops, demonstrations and dissemination activities. Contribute to research publications, patents and progress reports.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Shortlisted candidates are told about the interview only by email, so keep checking the primary email address you give in the form. The interview is held in person (physically) at NIT Delhi. No TA/DA is paid for attending. The decision of the expert interview panel, followed by approval from the competent authority, is final. The selected candidate has to join immediately.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The first appointment is for one year. It may be extended every year, up to a maximum of three (3) years, if performance is satisfactory and the project needs it. The position is purely temporary and lasts only as long as the project (co-terminus). It gives no claim to regular or permanent employment at the Institute. The appointment may be for a time-bound project, and the candidate must work with dedication to complete it successfully. The selected candidate may be encouraged to enrol for a Ph.D. This depends on the Institute's PhD ordinance and on whether PhD positions are available, or on the admission process at NIT Delhi. All terms and conditions follow ANRF guidelines and Institute norms.

faq.question: Q1. How much does the NIT Delhi Project Associate-I post pay?
faq.answer: It pays Rs. 37,000 plus HRA if you were selected through GATE or CSIR UGC NET, and Rs. 30,000 plus HRA if you were not.

faq.question: Q2. Is GATE compulsory for this post?
faq.answer: No. Candidates without GATE or CSIR UGC NET can apply, but they get Rs. 30,000 plus HRA instead of Rs. 37,000 plus HRA.

faq.question: Q3. Which B.Tech branches are eligible?
faq.answer: A four-year B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering or Computer Science Engineering, with first division/class.

faq.question: Q4. Will NIT Delhi provide accommodation?
faq.answer: No. Under the ANRF (PM-ECRG) project terms, HRA is paid instead, as per ANRF guidelines.

faq.question: Q5. How long is the appointment?
faq.answer: It is for one year at first. It may be extended every year up to three years, depending on performance and the project's needs.

faq.question: Q6. How will I know if I am shortlisted?
faq.answer: Shortlisted candidates are told only by email. The interview is in person at NIT Delhi, and no TA/DA is paid.

faq.question: Q7. In what format should the documents be uploaded?
faq.answer: Upload the signed application form and documents as one merged PDF with every page self-attested. Upload the photograph and signature as JPEG images.

faq.question: Q8. Can I do a Ph.D. while working on this project?
faq.answer: The selected candidate may be encouraged to enrol for a Ph.D. under the Institute's PhD ordinance, depending on PhD positions or the admission process at NIT Delhi.

faq.question: Q9. Who is the Principal Investigator of the project?
faq.answer: Dr. Navneet Garg, Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering. His email is [email protected].
